subject: Urban Planning
title: Floor Area Ratio: Density by Numbers
description: A short lesson to help you apply Floor Area Ratio: Density by Numbers.

hook.text: FAR is the ratio of total floor space to lot size. An FAR of 2 means you can build twice the lot area on that site.

buildup.text: A 10,000 sq ft lot with FAR 1 gets a one-story building. With FAR 10, you get a ten-story tower on the same lot.

discovery.text: FAR controls density invisibly. Low FARs in suburbs ban apartments without ever mentioning apartments directly.

twist.text: Developers buy unused FAR from neighboring buildings through 'air rights.' You can sell the sky above your roof.

climax.text: New York's supertall towers exist because developers bought air rights from short buildings nearby.

punchline.text: You can buy the air above a church. And build a skyscraper with it.

quiz.question: What are 'air rights' in urban development?
options: Government permits to emit a certain amount of air pollution
Unused building density that can be sold to neighboring properties
Rights to install rooftop antennas and communication towers
